transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-05
Start: 15:00 PT (57 min)
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Avery Chen (Redwood SE), Lena Brooks (Redwood Solutions), Dr. Maya Ruiz (CISO/Ivory), Rajat Singh (Platform Eng), Claire Holt (IT Ops), Ben Carter (Compliance)

Summary:
Quick security/compliance review focused on SSO onboarding (SAML), SCIM provisioning, tenant segmentation and least-privilege RBAC. Customer is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for regulated datasets. Discussed KMS/HSM integration, audit/logging, and SOC 2 artifacts. Agreed to follow-up technical workshop and send artifacts.

Topics covered:
- SSO: SAML IdP options, metadata exchange, Just-in-Time vs SCIM provisioning, session durations
- RBAC: role slicing, admin separation, least-privilege patterns across tenants
- Data residency & audit logs: retention, export, and alerting for access anomalies
- Encryption/KMS: customer-managed keys (KMS), HSM considerations, key rotation cadence
- Deployment considerations: Private VPC vs Dedicated pools for PHI workloads
Action items (captured above).

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate the tight schedule. I think the goal for today is to map out the SSO onboarding path and the access model so we can get your pilot running without surprises. Maya, do you want to kick off with your constraints?
[00:12] Dr. Maya Ruiz: Yeah hi, thanks. Our main thing is we handle PHI-ish clinical trial metadata, so we need clear data residency, audit trail, and KMS. We're using Okta as our IdP for now, plan to use SCIM for provisioning. Timeline is tight — pilot in three weeks if possible.
[00:30] Avery: Ok great. Three weeks is tight but doable for a hosted proof-of-concept; dedicated/private will need more provisioning lead time. We'll outline minimal steps: IdP metadata exchange, SCIM group mapping, role slice definitions, and test users.
[00:45] Rajat: Quick note — we run group-based role mapping today, but it's kinda flat. Want to move to role-slices per project/tenant. Also want to avoid giving engineers broad admin rights.
[01:02] Lena: Totally. We usually recommend a least-privilege matrix: operational admins, app managers, viewers, and a separate billing/owner role. For multi-tenant segmentation we can tie the tenant id claim to groups or attributes from Okta.
[01:22] Ben: From compliance side: we need immutable audit logs for all user activity, retention for 7 years, and proof of key management controls. SOC 2 is table stakes.
[01:35] Samir: Sounds good. We'll share our SOC 2 Type II and the architecture diagram. Quick question on KMS — do you want Redwood to manage keys or for you to bring your own?
[01:45] Dr. Maya Ruiz: Customer-managed KMS is preferred — we have an AWS KMS policy and a rotation cadence. If Private deploy is required for FIPS/HSM, we might go that route for the most sensitive datasets.
[02:05] Avery: We support both customer-managed KMS and our hosted keys. For customer-managed KMS we do envelope encryption: Redwood runtime has a data-encryption key wrapped by your KMS CMK. It works with cross-account roles. There was a small note though, sometimes the K V cache phrase shows up in docs as K V cash — auto-transcribe hiccup — but technically it's KV cache and session caching isn't encrypted end-to-end by default; we can enable cache encryption behind the KMS boundary.
[02:36] Rajat: Important detail: session TTLs. We need sessions to expire after 15 minutes for elevated roles and 8 hours for standard viewers. How granular are session policies?
[02:48] Avery: We can configure session timeouts per role via SAML assertions and map to Redwood session policies. For SCIM provisioning we can sync groups and a custom attribute for session_policy. Some IdPs allow transforming attributes — Okta's Rules or Azure AD claim mapping.
[03:12] Claire: What's the onboarding flow? Do you recommend Just-In-Time provisioning via SAML or full SCIM provisioning?
[03:21] Lena: For quick pilots JIT onboarding plus manual group assignment is fastest. For ongoing production we prefer SCIM with group sync so you don't have to manage users in two places. SCIM also allows deprovisioning which is important for least-privilege and audit.
[03:40] Dr. Maya Ruiz: Deprovisioning is non-negotiable from a compliance POV. Also want to ensure admin access is broken out — only a small operations team should have tenant-level admin.
[03:53] Samir: Understood. We'll propose role slices: Tenant Admin (limited to tenant config), Platform Admin (Redwood-managed for infra ops — can be scoped), Application Owner (can create prompts/flows), and ReadOnly/Auditor. Does that align?
[04:09] Rajat: Yes but we also need a cross-tenant support role that can view logs (masked) but not exfiltrate data.
[04:18] Avery: We can support masked log access and field-level redaction for PII in audit views. That does affect the logging pipeline — we should map which events are PII-sensitive and where to redact.
[04:36] Ben: On audit logs: we need tamper-evident logs and an append-only store with export capability for audits. Can Redwood provide signed logs or a chain of custody?
[04:50] Avery: We provide exportable logs and integration with CloudWatch/Stackdriver or an S3 bucket you control. For tamper-evidence we can optionally ship logs to an external immutability service or support syslog to your SIEM. We'll include recommended patterns in the follow-up doc.
[05:10] Dr. Maya Ruiz: Data residency — some datasets must remain in EU; others in US. How do we pin model routing or storage by region?
[05:21] Samir: Redwood routing can pin requests by policy: region-based routing, model variant selection in EU-only infra, and ensure KV cache and storage are in the selected region. For Private or Dedicated we can deploy a pool in your EU region.
[05:40] Rajat: For the pilot we want EU-only for certain tenants. We need a checklist of what to configure in the tenant to ensure no cross-region fallbacks.
[05:50] Lena: We'll provide a tenant configuration checklist that sets region pin, prevents fallback to global models, and configures data egress controls.
[06:03] Claire: Encryption questions: key rotation impacts access during rotation windows — any planned downtimes?
[06:11] Avery: With envelope encryption, rotation is seamless — we rewrap keys; there is no downtime for reads as long as you keep old wrapped keys available for a transition window. We'll document rotation cadence recommendations.
[06:28] Ben: Any SOC/ISO overlap we should call out? ISO27001 controls around access control maps nicely to RBAC proposals. We'll need control mappings for our internal audit.
[06:38] Samir: We'll include a control-mapping appendix tying Redwood features to SOC2/ISO controls (A.9 access control, etc.).
[06:46] Dr. Maya Ruiz: Also, can we get an architectural whiteboard showing where logs, keys, and IdP integrate?
[06:53] Lena: Yes, Avery will draft a wiring diagram showing SAML handshake, SCIM provisioning flow, KMS envelope encryption, and audit stream.
[07:03] Avery: One more thing: SCIM group names — we recommend using a stable naming convention: tenant-{tenant_id}-role-{role_name} so sync is idempotent and easy to script. Also recommend adding a claim for tenant_id in SAML so we can auto-assign tenant context.
[07:24] Rajat: Ok, we'll update our Okta mapping to include tenant_id custom attribute.
[07:30] Claire: In terms of least-privilege, do you support temporary elevation (break-glass) for emergency operations? We want time-limited elevated access with approval flows.
[07:41] Avery: We have built-in short-lived admin tokens for support scenarios, tied to audit and an approval workflow. For production we'd suggest requiring an approval step in your ITSM tool and pushing a proof-of-approval token into the request. We'll document integration points.
[07:59] Ben: Competitors question: we did a bake-off vs CloudEndpoints and VeloxAI. From compliance angle, their log retention and KMS story wasn't as flexible. Any gaps we should be aware of with Redwood?
[08:12] Samir: We try to be flexible; biggest gaps are around on-prem HSM integrations in very restricted air-gapped environments — that tends to increase lead time. For standard KMS and customer-managed keys we cover the major scenarios.
[08:30] Dr. Maya Ruiz: Great. Next steps recap?
[08:34] Samir: We'll share: SOC2 Type II, SSO + SCIM setup guide with example Okta metadata and claim mappings, tenant segmentation wiring diagram, RBAC role-slice proposal, and logging/retention playbook. We'll also schedule the technical workshop for the week of 10/12.
[08:55] Claire: For the pilot we'll confirm Okta metadata and group mappings by 10/09.
[09:01] Samir: Perfect — action items in the doc. Thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
